core.title: Re-open the plan session when a post-commit validator fails
core.given: A plan was ratified and its substrate committed.
core.then: Re-open the plan session, adjust the plan with the operator, and re-author it.
prefer: Make the adjustment together with the operator inside the re-opened session.
avoid: Leaving the validator failure unresolved instead of re-opening the session for adjustment and re-author.
core.why: The session's modify loop is how plan defects caught after commit are corrected: through operator adjustment and re-author.
evidence: After a post-commit validator failure, the session is re-opened and the plan is re-authored after operator adjustment.
verification: Enforcement scope follows activation: the check applies only to a validator failure occurring after the plan substrate of a ratified session was committed; the pre-ratification state (session still open) and work unrelated to a plan session are out of scope (activation.doesNotFire).

The finding fact has observability needs_new_observer: enforcing this rule requires the stack to realize an observer that links a post-commit validator failure to the ratified plan session; the core does not prescribe that observer.

values: post-commit validator failure on authored plan substrate

fires: A validator fails after the plan substrate was committed for a ratified session.
doesNotFire: Before ratification, while the plan session is still open (covered by the bind-before-ratify part).
Work unrelated to an ATDD plan session.

classification.note: Process-level condition over the plan artifact lifecycle; already neutral (no stack, path, or file-kind names).
Neutral trigger; 'validator' is generic, no realization named.
One obligation (the modify loop: re-open, adjust with the operator, re-author); carried verbatim.
Rationale stated in session-process terms; neutral.
Role/process-level preference (operator adjustment inside the re-opened session); no stack specifics to strip.
Negative form of the same obligation; neutral.
Observable restatement of the modify loop; neutral.

Per-rule severity and disposition are rule-level (notProfileKeys): mapped to the core's verification array, not to a profile key; no detector/validator id appears in bun.json, so nothing is bunOnly here.
Finding fact is neutral; observability needs_new_observer kept, and the missing observer is surfaced in core.verification.
Task terms contain no stack names; per notProfileKeys, rule-specific task terms belong to core activation when neutral.

neutralityNotes: bun.json states this convention entirely in plan-session process vocabulary (plan artifact, session, ratification, operator, validator); it names no stack, runtime, framework, package manager, path, or file suffix, so bunOnly and profileRequirements are empty and the core carries the texts essentially verbatim. The only neutralizations: 'Ratify/confirm' (which pairs the phase with the mechanical name of the ratify operation) is rendered as the ratification phase in doesNotFire, with identical scope; and the severity/disposition line moved into core.verification. The needs_new_observer fact means actual enforcement depends on a stack realizing an observer that links a post-commit validator failure to the ratified session; the core records that dependency instead of prescribing the observer.
